lessons.title: JavaScript Basics

content.title: What is JavaScript?
content.text: JavaScript is a programming language commonly used to add interactivity and dynamic behavior to web pages. It can run in browsers and also on servers using environments such as Node.js.

content.title: JavaScript Syntax
content.text: JavaScript programs consist of statements and expressions. Statements can be separated using semicolons, although semicolons are often optional because JavaScript has automatic semicolon insertion.

content.title: Hello World
content.code: console.log("Hello, World!");

content.title: Variables
content.text: Variables store values. Modern JavaScript commonly uses let for values that may change and const for values that should not be reassigned.

content.title: Variables

key_points: JavaScript adds behavior and interactivity to web applications.
console.log() can display information.
let is used for variables that may be reassigned.
const is used for bindings that should not be reassigned.

lessons.title: Data Types and Operators

content.title: Common Data Types
content.text: Common JavaScript data types include string, number, boolean, undefined, null, object and symbol. BigInt is also available for integers outside the safe range of Number.

content.title: Data Types
Arithmetic Operators
content.text: JavaScript supports arithmetic operators such as +, -, *, / and %.

content.title: Arithmetic
Comparison Operators
content.text: Comparison operators compare values. Strict equality === checks both value and type, while strict inequality !== checks that either value or type differs.

key_points: JavaScript has several primitive data types.
typeof can be used to inspect a value's type.
Arithmetic operators perform mathematical operations.
Prefer strict equality === when comparing values.

lessons.title: Conditions and Loops

content.title: Conditional Statements
content.text: Conditional statements allow a program to execute different code depending on whether a condition is true or false.

content.title: If Else
Switch
content.text: A switch statement can be useful when comparing one expression against multiple possible cases.

content.title: Switch
Loops
content.text: Loops repeat code. Common JavaScript loops include for, while and for...of.

content.title: For Loop

key_points: if and else execute code conditionally.
switch handles multiple possible cases.
for loops are useful when the number of iterations is known.
while loops continue while a condition is true.

lessons.title: Functions

content.title: What is a Function?
content.text: A function is a reusable block of code designed to perform a particular task.

content.title: Basic Function
Parameters
content.text: Parameters allow functions to receive input values. A return statement sends a result back to the caller.

content.title: Function Parameters
Arrow Functions
content.text: Arrow functions provide a shorter syntax for writing functions and are commonly used with array methods.

content.title: Arrow Function
content.code:
const square = (number) => number * number;

console.log(square(5));

key_points: Functions allow code reuse.
Parameters provide input.
return provides an output.
Arrow functions provide concise function syntax.

lessons.title: Arrays

content.title: What is an Array?
content.text: An array is an ordered collection of values. Array indexes start at zero.

content.title: Creating an Array
Adding Items
content.text: The push() method adds one or more elements to the end of an array.

content.title: Push
Map
content.text: map() creates a new array by applying a function to each element.

content.title: Map
Filter
content.text: filter() creates a new array containing elements that satisfy a condition.

key_points: Array indexes begin at zero.
length gives the number of elements.
push() adds elements to the end.
map() transforms array elements.
filter() selects elements based on a condition.

lessons.title: Objects

content.title: What is an Object?
content.text: An object stores related data using key-value pairs. Objects are commonly used to represent entities such as users, products and employees.

content.title: Object
Changing Properties
content.text: Properties of an object can be accessed and changed using dot notation or bracket notation.

content.title: Updating an Object
Object Methods
content.text: A function stored as an object property is commonly called a method.

key_points: Objects store key-value pairs.
Properties can be accessed using dot notation.
Object properties can be changed.
Objects can contain functions as methods.

lessons.title: DOM Manipulation and Events

content.title: What is the DOM?
content.text: The Document Object Model represents an HTML document as a tree of objects. JavaScript can use the DOM to read and modify page content.

content.title: Selecting an Element
content.code:
const heading = document.querySelector("h1");
heading.textContent = "Welcome!";

content.title: Changing Styles
content.text: JavaScript can modify an element's properties and styles through the DOM.

content.title: Changing a Style
content.code:
const heading = document.querySelector("h1");
heading.style.color = "blue";

content.title: Events
content.text: Events occur when users or the browser perform actions such as clicking, typing or submitting a form.

content.title: Click Event

key_points: The DOM represents an HTML document as objects.
querySelector() can select elements.
textContent can change text.
addEventListener() can respond to events.

lessons.title: Modern JavaScript Basics

content.title: Template Literals
content.text: Template literals use backticks and allow expressions to be embedded using ${}.

content.title: Template Literal
Destructuring
content.text: Destructuring allows values to be extracted from arrays or properties from objects into variables.

content.title: Object Destructuring
Spread Syntax
content.text: The spread operator ... can expand elements from arrays or properties from objects.

content.title: Spread

key_points: Template literals make string interpolation easier.
Destructuring extracts values conveniently.
Spread syntax expands arrays or objects.
Modern JavaScript provides concise syntax for common operations.
